❭ where does the proxy add the customer headers?

 … 2 earlier steps
 ✓ Search for 'proxy|/api'
 ✓ Search for 'x-customer|customer_id|customer-id|header'
 … Reading ./src/proxy.js
 ✓ Read file

 In  src/proxy.js , in  toUpstreamInit()  (line 5). Every proxied request gets a fresh headers object containing hardcoded
 customer identity headers:


   const headers = { 'X-User-Id': 'cust-ana', 'X-User-Role': 'CUSTOMER' };


 It then copies only  content-type  and  content-length  from the incoming request (lines 6–8) — so the client can't override
 or inject its own  X-User-Id , and the value is always  cust-ana  regardless of who's actually logged in.  proxyRequest()
 (line 26) passes that init object straight to  fetch(api + req.url, ...) .  server.js  mounts this on  /api  requests.
 Worth noting: if the bug you're chasing is "portal always shows Ana's claims," this is why — the proxy stamps a fixed customer
 ID on every upstream call.
